items.note: Dhār image inscription, V.S. 1138 (1081 A.C.), consecration of a Devī image; king taken to be Udayāditya from the find-spot, known from the Udaipur inscription dated a year before.
Inscription of Udayāditya's time: Naravarman, evidently his son, donates 12 halas of land to burn a lamp for Lakshmadēva; Udayāditya encamped at Dhavalī near Ujjain; year 1140 (1082 A.C.).
Lakshmadēva and Naravarman are well-known sons of Udayāditya; the expression 'akshaya-dīpikā' implies Lakshmadēva had died shortly before.
New fact that Lakshmadēva predeceased both Udayāditya and Naravarman; omission of a royal title suggests he never ascended the throne of Dhāra; he perhaps governed in the eastern Paramāra dominions.

items.note: Jhālrapātan inscription: date Samvat 1143 (26 April 1086 A.C. or 1087), names Udayādityadēva as prosperous in the region, and records the construction of a Śambhu temple by the pattakila Jannaka.
Same Jannaka excavated a stepped well in Chirihilla between Ghōshakupikā and Vruvāsaka.
Temple built and record put up while Udayāditya was ruling the region; his identity as the Paramāra of Dhāra is clear from the Udaipur inscription of V.S. 1137, six years earlier.
Jannaka promised four palas of oil and a ball of sweets yearly for Śrī-Lōligasvāmidēva; a small temple endowment.
Udayāditya's kingdom, which recovered Mālwā, included the region up to Jhālrapātan and Kōtā and 'a part of the modern District of Vidishā in the north-east'.
